about: The Jetsam packet schema, version 1.0 (J1, the atlas's TODO-193). A packet is one framework's digest of one epoch from one house: counts of named events, nothing else (JETSAM, The packet). Its bytes and its name follow the atlas's kernel-format core v1: canonical JSON (RFC 8785 under the core's profile), named by its full SHA-256 content hash. src/jetsam/validate.py reads this file; nothing else defines the packet.
classes_ruled: JT.16 (the operator's word, AT.555): all ten classes, P0, P1 and P2, declared in 1.0, so no class bump is needed later. A recorder still offers only what its consent screen and its train carry.
lists_unmeasured_why: P2's scales are fixed here before any house has measured a cost (JT.16 named the risk). Each is a doubling scale; a house's first measured epochs show whether its cells fall where the scale can tell them apart, and a change to a scale is a schema bump.

kinds.id:<lists>: an id from the packet's framework's enum file, in one of the named lists; |null admits null
kinds.step: a step id of the event's funnel, as its enum entry declares; null exactly when the funnel declares no steps
kinds.integer: the number of steps the event's funnel declares (0 when it declares none)
kinds.list:<name>: a value from the named closed list above
kinds.wall: the wall the enum file declares for the event's tool
kinds.attached: an id from the list the event's `attached` names: funnels, gates or checks
kinds.release: a release id from the packet's framework's release list, never dev

text.rule: null unless the packet carries its one suggestion event; then the suggestion's text, scrubbed in the house, shown and confirmed, and refused here if the scrubber would still remove anything (JT.3)

pseudonym.form: 64 lowercase hex, or null when the operator has not turned it on (JT.2)
pseudonym.rule: kernel-format's salted commitment (core A8): SHA-256 over the tag, one 0x00 byte, the house's 32-byte secret for this framework, and the epoch's UTF-8 bytes; the secret never leaves jetsam/local/

order: classes in this file's class order, each once; events sorted by their canonical bytes, and no two events alike but for their count, so the order of events and their splitting carry nothing about when they happened
never: paths, hostnames, addresses, timestamps finer than a month, names, director labels, the canary, agent ids, session ids, close tokens, item texts, ledger lines, recall questions or answers, worldview contents, anything from a soul's data folder or the Tenant, model outputs, prompts, and anything a participant in the Membrane's study did: no field of this schema can hold them
